references.text: Earlier in the story, the Lord opened the donkey's mouth, preparing for the confrontation with the angel who now speaks to Balaam.
The three times Balaam struck the donkey, which the angel now confronts him about.
The Lord's angel stood on the road as an adversary (satan) against Balaam, something that is now explained directly to him.
Satan as an adversary who stands before the Lord, a similar use of the term 'satan' for an opponent.
Satan as a heavenly adversary, parallel to the angel's role as an adversary on the road.
Satan as an adversary against Israel; the same Hebrew root is used for the role of adversary.
The use of 'satan' as accuser or adversary.
Satan as an adversary in a heavenly scene, parallel use of the term for a spiritual opponent.
Peter's words refer to Balaam's way and how he was rebuked for his transgression.
